reason: Verified per-site (RFC 0106): `uri.path` (`connection_url_resolver.rb:94-100`) — WHATWG `URL` spells the path component `pathname`, so no `path` call is emitted.

Verified per-site (RFC 0106): `uri_parser.parse(url)` (`connection_url_resolver.rb:27`) — `URI::RFC2396_Parser` splits opaque (`scheme:path`) from hierarchical URIs, which WHATWG `new URL()` does not, so the constructor splits the scheme itself and only reaches `new URL()` for the hierarchical arm.

Verified per-site (RFC 0106): `@uri.query` (`connection_url_resolver.rb:32`) — WHATWG `URL` spells the query component `search` (leading `?` included), so there is no `query` call for the comparator to credit.

Name-collision false positive (story relation-delegation-rails-named-methods): exposing the `delegate ... to: :records` set under Rails names made `split`/`reverse`/`rindex` recognized ported method names, so this unrelated call to String#split / Array#reverse / String#rindex on a non-Relation receiver is flagged by the name-based wide call-set check.

Verified per-site (RFC 0106): `query_hash.merge(...)` / `.reverse_merge(...)` (`connection_url_resolver.rb:64-77`) — a non-mutating Hash merge is an object spread in TS; the two precedences are the two spread orders.
